Repaired the one verified finding: FIG. 2 did not depict the controller-to-connector-current-sensor coupling that claim 1 and the detailed description recite. Only `figures/FIG-2.md` changes; claims, description, numeral table and the other briefs are untouched.

On routing: the gate's suggested fix (a line leaving the circle leftward and out the left side below the bus) cannot be drawn in this figure without crossing the bus line, the bus branch to the contactor, or the control-pilot-interface-to-vehicle-connector link — the sensor sits on the power run to the right of the contactor, and the bus and pilot links occupy the whole region between it and the left side. I therefore took the sensing path straight up and out of the top of the channel boundary, parallel to and clear of the incoming supply line. That satisfies the substance of the fix — a separate sensing path from sensor 124 to the edge controller, not attached to the isolated local bus (the disclosure limits that bus to the interfaces and contactors) — with no crossings and no free-standing geometry idiom that the figure set does not already use (the supply line and the bus line both terminate at free ends in this drawing).

FIG. 1 was left alone deliberately: its connector channels are opaque blocks, and per-channel sensing lines cannot be added there without crossing the bus branches. The finding scoped the depiction gap to the FIG. 2 detail view.

Per the drafting brief: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art in `prior_art/` may be incomplete; nothing in this repair depends on it.

input.summary: Fixed all four verified findings with minimal, surgical patches across three files. (1) Removed the unsupported topology assertion that the connector-current sensing path is separate from and not joined to the isolated local bus — the exclusivity clause is deleted from figures/FIG-2.md and the closed enumeration of the bus payload in the detailed description is reopened with "including", while the plain coupling lines in FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 and the description's coupling sentence are retained unchanged; for the same reason "A separate solid line" in the FIG-2 sensing paragraph became "A further solid line" so the word "separate" cannot be read as a topology claim. (2) Resolved the FIG-2 self-contradiction by ending the sensing line at a free end well inside the drawing area and clear of the filing margins, matching the FIG. 1 convention. (3) Removed the double use of numeral 124 by making the FIG. 3 paragraph refer to the connector current sensor of each connector channel generically, with 124 cited only as the example shown in FIG. 2. (4) Added the controller-to-connector-current-sensor coupling to the Summary so it matches claim 1's four-way coupling recitation. No claim, numeral-table, or embodiment text was altered, and no rendered artifact was touched — the FIG-2 geometry change is made only in the authoritative Markdown brief so the pipeline re-renders and re-inspects fresh pixels. Note carried forward from the brief: no prior-art search was run, so the art considered may be incomplete.

figures/FIG-2.md: changed 'A separate solid line' to 'A further solid line' in the sensing-line paragraph so no wording characterizes the sensing path as independent of the control bus.

figures/FIG-2.md: the sensing line now ends at a free end well inside the upper part of the drawing area, clear of the filing margins, instead of at the drawing-area boundary, resolving the contradiction with the brief's own margin constraint.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: the isolated local bus 108 sentence now reads as an open, non-exhaustive enumeration ('carries communications ... including'), so the bus payload is no longer stated to exclude connector current measurements.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: FIG. 3 paragraph no longer applies numeral 124 to the sensor of every connector channel; it refers to 'the connector current sensor of each connector channel, such as the connector current sensor 124 shown in FIG. 2', so numeral 124 designates only the first channel's sensor.
draft/06-summary.md: the controller coupling sentence now recites the connector current sensors alongside the control-pilot interfaces, contactors and branch current sensor, matching claim 1.

patches.find: A separate solid line leaves the top of the circle outline and runs straight upward, parallel to the incoming vertical line and to the right of it, crosses the top side of the dashed rectangle, and continues upward to end at the upper boundary of the drawing area, as the connection that leads to the edge controller of FIG. 3.
patches.replace: A further solid line leaves the top of the circle outline and runs straight upward, parallel to the incoming vertical line and to the right of it, crosses the top side of the dashed rectangle, and continues upward to end at a free end well inside the upper part of the drawing area and clear of the filing margins, as the connection that leads to the edge controller of FIG. 3.
patches.why: Fixes the FIG-2 margin contradiction: the brief required all line work to stay well inside the drawing area clear of the filing margins, yet told this line to terminate at the drawing-area boundary. The free end well inside the area follows the convention FIG. 1 already uses for the incoming supply. 'A separate' becomes 'A further' so the sentence describes only line-work sequence and cannot be read as asserting a sensing path independent of the isolated local bus.

patches.find: It runs clear of the contactor outline, of the incoming vertical line and of the vehicle connector block, it neither touches nor joins the isolated local bus line, and it crosses no other line work.
patches.replace: It runs clear of the contactor outline, of the incoming vertical line and of the vehicle connector block, and it crosses no other line work.
patches.why: Removes the affirmative exclusivity statement that the sensing path does not join the isolated local bus. No inventor passage describes how connector current readings reach the controller; the disclosure's bus sentence enumerates only the connector interfaces and contactors and is silent on the sensors. The plain coupling line remains, which is a permissible drawing convention for the inherently disclosed verification coupling.

patches.find: The isolated local bus 108 carries, between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.
patches.replace: The isolated local bus 108 carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.
patches.why: The closed enumeration implied that the bus does not carry the connector current measurements, reinforcing the same unsupported exclusion found in the FIG-2 brief. The open form keeps every disclosed payload while no longer excluding anything the inventor did not exclude.

patches.find: and to the connector current sensor 124 of each connector channel, shown in FIG. 2.
patches.replace: and to the connector current sensor of each connector channel, such as the connector current sensor 124 shown in FIG. 2.
patches.why: Numeral 124 is introduced in the FIG. 2 discussion as the connector current sensor of the first connector channel 120 and is listed once in the numeral table. Attaching it to the sensor of every connector channel made one numeral designate more than one part. The generic form matches the usage already adopted elsewhere in the description ('the connector current sensor of that connector channel').

patches.find: A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor.
patches.replace: A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the connector current sensors, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor.
patches.why: Claim 1 recites the controller as coupled to four things including the connector current sensors; the Summary recited only three, stating a narrower coupling than the claim it summarizes. The Detailed Description already supports the coupling ('The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel'), and the coupling is traceable to the disclosed verification step, so this is a consistency repair only.

2

The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The isolated local bus 108 reaches the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. The edge controller 106 stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current requested for the session at that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the edge controller 106 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1, and to the connector current sensor of each connector channel, such as the connector current sensor 124 shown in FIG. 2.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18

The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.
22	
23	At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.
24	
25	At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.
26	
27	At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 receives a measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 and compares the measured branch current with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.
28	
29	At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
30	
31	The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current that remains above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
32	
33	At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.
34	
35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.
36	
37	The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.
38	
39	During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.
40	
41	Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.
42	
43	The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected when the association is carried out, rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.
44	
45	The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Reclosure of the contactor is withheld until the three conditions are satisfied together, and a connector channel whose contactor has been reclosed takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected when the association is carried out, rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.
